phase: ROADMAP Stage 5: outcome metrics logging + summary skeleton v1 (adoption rate, edit distance, completion time, rework rounds; synthetic fixture only)
summary: Added a deterministic, stdlib-only Stage 5 outcome-metrics skeleton. load_outcome_metrics_log loads a {metadata, rows} log; validate_outcome_metrics_log checks per case_id/arm_id identity, numeric ranges, and ISO-like timestamps when duration is absent (missing optional metrics warn, malformed required identity errors); summarize_outcome_metrics derives adoption_rate (accepted bool or accepted_sections/total_sections), edit_distance (stdlib Levenshtein when draft/final text supplied, else supplied numeric), duration_seconds (supplied or completed_at-started_at), and rework_rounds, then aggregates per arm and overall. A CLI tools/validate_outcome_metrics.py validates and optionally summarizes. Synthetic fixture only; no persistence, no real data, no model call, no network.
implemented: backend/server.py: added load_outcome_metrics_log(path) (raises ValueError on non-object / missing rows).

backend/server.py: added _levenshtein(a, b) stdlib edit distance, _parse_iso_timestamp(value) (handles trailing Z), and _outcome_row_metrics(row) deriving adoption_rate/edit_distance/duration_seconds/rework_rounds.

backend/server.py: added validate_outcome_metrics_log(log) returning {passed, errors, warnings, row_count, arm_ids}; enforces case_id/arm_id identity + uniqueness, accepted/section/edit/duration/rework types and ranges, and ISO-like timestamps (completed >= started) when duration absent; warns on missing optional metrics.
backend/server.py: added summarize_outcome_metrics(log) with method=outcome_metrics_summary_v1; per-row metrics plus per-arm and overall means (only present metrics contribute; None when absent).
tools/validate_outcome_metrics.py: CLI (--log/--json, optional --summary) delegating to the server helpers; exit 0/1/2.
tests/data/outcome_metrics_sample.json: synthetic 4-row fixture exercising accepted-bool, section-ratio, computed vs supplied edit distance, and timestamp vs supplied duration modes.
tests/test_outcome_metrics.py: 15 tests across validation, summary, Levenshtein, and the CLI.
tools/run_quality_gates.py: py-compile gate now includes tests/test_outcome_metrics.py and tools/validate_outcome_metrics.py.
README.md and docs/ROADMAP.md document the v1 boundary; only the ROADMAP '记录采纳率、修改距离、完成时间、返工轮次' item is marked done (regression-run automation untouched).
not_implemented: No persistence DB or UI; the log is a request-local JSON document.
No real human/model usage data; the fixture is synthetic placeholder data.
No regression-run automation (that Stage 5 item remains unchecked).
No causal, significance, or reviewer-agreement analysis; means only. No model call or network.

risks: Edit distance is character-level Levenshtein; it is O(len(draft)*len(final)) and scales poorly for very large documents (fine for the skeleton's short texts). It measures literal edits, not semantic change.
Duration from timestamps assumes started_at/completed_at share a timezone context; naive (no-offset) timestamps are treated as-is, so a caller mixing naive and aware timestamps could mis-measure.
Aggregates are simple means over present values only; a metric absent on some rows still averages the rows that have it, which can bias per-arm comparisons.
Fixtures are synthetic placeholder data and must not be mistaken for real usage telemetry.

Environment note: the local interpreter is python3 (no bare 'python' on PATH); the quality-gate runner honors PYTHON=python3, and a local 'python->python3' PATH shim lets its default-interpreter meta-test pass.
